newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX ACCESS crude prices rise on API draw.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX ACCESS crude prices rise on API draw.

text.p: U.S. crude oil futures rose moderately in thin ACCESS trade, supported by new data on Tuesday that showed a draw in nationwide crude stocks.

Traders said ACCESS prices reacted slowly to the weekly inventory report from the American Petroleum Institute (API). The trade group said crude on hand at U.S. refiners dropped a sharp 5.9 million barrels.
Players discounted the dramatic change, saying the draw was a reversal of questionable 6.9 million-barrel build reported last week.

"There wasn't much of a reaction initially," one trader said, noting the new front-month contract, July, rose as high as $21.80 a barrel before slipping back to $21.75, about 16 cents a barrel over the daytime close.
Several hours into ACCESS, 953 lots traded for July crude oil Tuesday, with 1,187 overall.
Traders saw crude oil resistance at $22.15 Wednesday, with support at $21.50 a barrel.
June unleaded gasoline eased to 65.35 a gallon, off a mere 0.04 cents from the settle as 122 lots changed hands in July and 208 overall.
"Products are neutral to bearish," a trader said, with heating oil demand slack because of warmer weather and gasoline stocks reported up 837,000 barrels.
But a draw in reformulated gasoline stocks, which fell 1.4 million barrels, could put a "pop" in futures prices Wednesday, one trader said.
June heating oil fell 0.16 cents a gallon afterhours to 57.80 cents. June volume for heating oil stood 28 with 105 lots traded in all months.
